contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you proved two triangles congruent using just three pieces of information. Today, the powerful payoff: what does that proof tell you about everything else?

CPCTC stands for 'Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent.' Once you've proven two triangles congruent — by any method, SSS, SAS, or ASA — EVERY corresponding side and angle must also be equal, even the ones you never directly used in the proof. In yesterday's proof, Triangle ABD ≅ Triangle CBD was proven using SAS (AB=CB, angle ABD=angle CBD, BD=BD). By CPCTC, this also proves AD = CD and angle ADB = angle CDB — parts never directly compared in the original proof. This is genuinely useful: proving congruence with just 3 pieces of information unlocks certainty about ALL 6 corresponding parts. Using yesterday's proof, state one additional fact CPCTC now guarantees that wasn't part of the original given information.
You just used CPCTC to unlock new facts from an already-completed proof. Tomorrow we'll review everything about congruence and proof from this whole week.

objectives: Define CPCTC and explain when it applies
Apply CPCTC to derive a new fact from an already-proven congruence
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's completed proof.
2. Introduce CPCTC and why it's a genuinely powerful follow-up tool.
3. Apply CPCTC to yesterday's proof together, deriving AD=CD.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one new fact (AD=CD) rather than requiring the child to find all remaining corresponding parts
Ready for more: ask them to list ALL 6 corresponding parts (3 sides, 3 angles) for yesterday's two triangles, noting which 3 were given/proven directly and which 3 come from CPCTC
Emphasize that CPCTC only applies AFTER congruence has already been proven — it can't be used to prove the congruence itself, only to use it afterward
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. CPCTC means Corresponding Parts of Congruent Triangles are Congruent. 2. It applies only after triangles have already been proven congruent. 3. From yesterday's proof, CPCTC guarantees AD=CD (and angle ADB=angle CDB), neither of which was directly given or used in the proof.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Geometry standard G-CO.10, extending the practical value of a completed congruence proof — a genuine 'why does this matter' payoff for the week's proof-writing skill.

rows.problem: From the Triangle ABD ≅ Triangle CBD proof, what does CPCTC guarantee about AD and CD?
